_readme: Hand-written English boundary-case eval set for structure()/buildSystemPromptEn in functions/src/index.ts. Each case is a spoken-style transcript with the classification a human would expect. Run manually through structure() (or the deployed callable) and compare notes[].category/tasks[] against `expected`. category values match the internal literal strings the prompt outputs: 'アイデア' (idea) or '感情ログ' (diary/emotion-log); tasks go to the top-level tasks[] array.

cases.transcript: I need to call the dentist tomorrow morning to reschedule my appointment.
cases.why: Unambiguous confirmed action with explicit timing — sanity check, not a boundary case.

cases.transcript: What if I turned the spare bedroom into a little reading nook with a hammock chair?
cases.why: Unconfirmed speculative idea, no action taken — sanity check.

cases.transcript: Today was rough. My manager criticized my work in front of everyone and I just felt so small.
cases.why: Pure feeling/reflection, no idea or action — sanity check.

cases.transcript: Ugh, the kitchen faucet is still leaking, I really need to fix that this weekend.
cases.why: Complaint ('ugh', 'still leaking') wraps a confirmed action with timing. Risk: model treats the whole thing as emotion-log and drops the task, or vice versa drops the frustration.

cases.transcript: I'm so tired of doing the dishes every night, I should really just buy a dishwasher already.
cases.why: Venting ('so tired of') followed by a soft-but-real intention ('should really just buy'). Ambiguous whether 'should' counts as confirmed action per the prompt's rule.

cases.transcript: I'm so tired of doing the dishes every night, it never ends.
cases.why: Near-identical wording to the previous case but with the action clause removed — checks the model isn't pattern-matching 'tired of X' into an automatic task.

cases.transcript: I wish I lived closer to the ocean, it would make weekends so much better.
cases.why: 'I wish' sounds idea-shaped but is really a feeling about current circumstances with no actionable/considerable plan — should land in emotion-log, not idea.

cases.transcript: I've been thinking maybe I should move somewhere closer to the ocean, like actually looking into it.
cases.why: Near-identical topic to the previous case, but 'actually looking into it' signals genuine consideration, not just longing — should land in idea, not emotion-log. Pair with idea-vs-diary-wish-01 to test the model isn't relying on surface keywords like 'wish'.

cases.transcript: Maybe I'll start learning Spanish this year, not sure when though.
cases.why: 'Maybe' + no committed timing = unconfirmed idea, not a task, despite sounding intention-like.

cases.transcript: I'm starting Spanish lessons next Monday, I already signed up.
cases.why: Same topic area as previous case but committed + already acted on + has timing — should be a task, tests the model distinguishes 'maybe' from 'already signed up'.

cases.transcript: Okay so I need to pick up dry cleaning by Friday, and also, kind of randomly, I was thinking it might be cool to start a small herb garden on the balcony. Also today was actually a pretty good day, I felt proud of finishing that project.
cases.why: Three distinct topics in one breath (task/idea/diary) — checks correct splitting into 3 entries rather than merging or dropping one.

cases.transcript: I have a doctor's appointment Thursday at 3pm, and I also need to call my sister back, she's called twice.
cases.why: Two separate tasks in one utterance with different timing granularity (specific time vs no time) — checks both get split out instead of merged into one task.

cases.transcript: Oh great, ANOTHER email from my landlord about the rent increase, love that for me.
cases.why: Sarcasm ('love that for me') could confuse sentiment/emotion tagging; no actual task stated even though a landlord/rent topic often correlates with tasks.

cases.transcript: Rent's due on the first, and I still haven't transferred the money.
cases.why: No explicit 'I need to' — action must be inferred from 'still haven't' + a deadline. Tests inference rule #2 in the prompt (infer missing subject/timing/action).

cases.transcript: That was such a stressful meeting, I'm never doing another product launch without a written agenda again.
cases.why: 'I'm never doing X without Y' reads like a resolution/idea but is really a reflective takeaway about a past event with no concrete near-term action or plan — should stay diary, not idea or task.

cases.transcript: That meeting was a mess. Next time I'm going to draft the agenda myself and send it out two days early.
cases.why: Same emotional framing as previous case, but pairs it with a concrete recurring intention ('next time I'm going to X') — arguably a task/habit, tests whether the model over-generalizes 'reflection = diary only'.

cases.transcript: Should I even keep this gym membership? I haven't gone in like two months.
cases.why: A genuine open question/consideration with no decision made — idea category ('something to consider'), not a task (no decision to cancel yet) and not pure emotion (it's deliberative, not just venting).

cases.transcript: Why does it always rain the one day I decide to walk to work?
cases.why: Grammatically a question like the previous case, but rhetorical/venting rather than a genuine open consideration — tests the model isn't classifying by sentence type (question mark) instead of intent.

cases.transcript: Um, so, like, I think, um, I need to, uh, finish the, um, the tax stuff, like, by the end of the month I guess.
cases.why: Heavy filler words should be stripped per prompt rule #1 while still extracting the one real task with its deadline.

cases.transcript: I need to book the flights, I need to book the flights before prices go up, seriously I need to book the flights.
cases.why: Exact repeated phrase (likely a recording/re-take artifact) should collapse into a single task, not three duplicate tasks.

cases.transcript: I'm really grateful my friend helped me move this weekend, it made me think I should do something nice for her.
cases.why: Gratitude (diary) plus a vague not-yet-planned idea ('should do something nice') in the same breath — tests correct splitting rather than forcing one category over the other, and that the vague idea isn't upgraded to a task without any concrete plan.

cases.transcript: I'm really worried about the presentation next week, I don't feel ready at all.
cases.why: Anxiety about an upcoming known event with no stated action ('don't feel ready') — should not be inflated into a task like 'prepare for presentation' since no action was actually stated, tests over-inference.

cases.transcript: I'm really worried about the presentation next week, so I'm going to run through my slides with Sarah on Tuesday.
cases.why: Same worry framing as previous case but now paired with a concrete planned action + day — should split into task + diary, contrasts with worry-vs-task-01 to check the model isn't auto-generating a task purely from anxiety language.

cases.transcript: Dentist. Friday. Don't forget.
cases.why: Extremely terse, fragment-style speech (as if talking to oneself in a hurry) — tests robustness to non-sentence input still yielding a correct task with timing.

cases.transcript: I need to email the landlord about the, uh, how do you say, deposit reembolso, before Friday.
cases.why: Brief code-switch into Spanish mid-sentence (common for bilingual speakers) — output must still be English per the prompt's output-language rule, and the task should still be extracted correctly.

cases.transcript: So I was just thinking about this the whole walk home, like, work has been fine I guess, nothing bad happened today really, but I don't know, I've just been feeling kind of empty lately, like going through the motions, and I can't really point to why.
cases.why: Long rambling monologue but genuinely a single topic (a diffuse mood, not tied to one event) — tests the model doesn't over-split a single feeling into multiple fragmented diary entries just because it's long.

cases.transcript: I decided I'm NOT going to redo the whole bathroom this year, it's just not worth the stress right now.
cases.why: Explicit decision to NOT do something — must not be misread as a task ('redo the bathroom') by keying off the noun phrase while ignoring the negation.

cases.transcript: If I ever get a raise, I think I'd want to finally get a good office chair, my back has been killing me.
cases.why: Conditional/hypothetical purchase idea gated on an uncertain future event, plus a real current physical complaint — tests that the conditional idea isn't promoted to a task, and that the two parts (idea + diary) get split.
